# Module source parameter acceptance

Use an isolated profile and background headless processes. Disable Pointer Lock
at initialization; do not synthesize mouse/keyboard input or focus windows.

1. Install two instances of the pinned Kenney building source package into a
   creation world and place them separately with the ordinary source transaction.
2. Capture instance A through the host's current scene-object selection. Read
   `module-parameters`; compare source values, source pin, package instance,
   entity and runtime identity. Confirm there is no draft lease or source write.
3. Request a changed scale, rotation, solidity or metadata label using that
   binding hash. Require a single parent scene operation with expected hash,
   unchanged instance B/shared resource bytes, and explicit unassessed safety.
4. Apply through the ordinary patch/check/adoption flow. Verify actual visual
   scale, orientation and collision separately, then save and cold-open. Verify
   the same parameter values, player progress, inventory and unaffected peer.
5. Export A, install into a second world and re-export. Require the preserved
   original parameter declaration and local overrides, with new source identity.
6. Change source, replace the runtime instance or use a stale binding; require
   refusal before any write. Test duplicate IDs, altered wrapper bytes, inherited
   scenes and shared resource requests. A no-op must not create a check job.

Pure fixtures and real Core source transactions cover only the stages they
actually execute. Synthetic captures are not live host or physics evidence.
Plugin-bundle tests are not sealed-client acceptance. The existing catalog's
25-step sealed test predates these modes and cannot prove them. An ordinary
player-model test remains separate and must use the user's confirmed model and
thinking setting, without additional token, call-count or whole-turn limits.
